simple.meaning: אֲנָךְ (ʼănâk) is a Hebrew word meaning “according to most a plumb-line , and to others a hook.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: אֲנָךְ (H594) appears 4 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Amos 7:7, with occurrences in Amos.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to אֲנָךְ (H594) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in אֲנָךְ (H594) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: אֲנָךְ (ʼănâk) / H594 is traced through Amos 7:7, Amos 7:8 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.short: according to most a plumb-line , and to others a hook
definitions.full: H594. anak אֲנָךְ noun [masculine] plummet (compare words in cognate languages for lead, tin , etymology dubious, perhaps foreign; Arabic (see Frä 153 ) Syriac Mandean אנכא , Assyrian anâku Lyon Sargontexte 92 ; see Lag Arm. Stud. § 103 compare Id. BN 175 ) — אֲנָ֑ךְ except once Amos 7:8 — plummet 7:7-8 , (twice in verse); א ׳חוֺמַת , i.e. a vertical wall vAmos 7:7.
definitions.rootNote: probably from an unused root meaning to be narrow;
